payload.claim: The comment on this except-clause (lines 124-126) asserts a raise from `runner` is 'never charged to a task, because no task was ever started for it' — but `run_one_cell` (saffron/cell/session.py) creates `run_id`/`task_id` at lines 824-839, opens the phase loop's try block at line 855, and only its outermost `except BaseException: ... raise` (session.py:1765-1775) is what actually reaches this except-clause. That try block spans `plan_checkpoint` and every later phase, so a crash after one or more attempts have already opened and closed with real `cost_usd_est` (e.g. a runtime dying mid-REPAIR) still propagates as a raised exception. Because `run_batch` never learns that run's `run_id` on this path, `attach_run_to_batch` is never called, the run's `batch_id` stays NULL forever, and `ledger.batch_spend` (which sums attempts joined through `runs.batch_id`) permanently excludes real, already-spent money from the budget gate at line 108 — letting the batch admit further candidates against a budget that is actually already partly consumed. No test here catches this because `FakeRunner` raises a bare exception with no ledger rows behind it at all, unlike the real failure mode.
